title: Faithfully flat localization-completion cover
statement: Let $A$ be a reduced Noetherian commutative ring and let $0\ne f\in A$. Here $A_f$ is the localization away from $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Let $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_n A/(f^n)$ be the $f$-adic completion. Then the canonical map $A\to A_f\times A^\wedge$ is faithfully flat [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Tag 05FS, lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective, proof: the map R to R_f times R-hat is faithfully flat (using Algebra Tag 00MB, lemma-completion-flat)

proof.text: Put $C=A^\wedge$ and $B=A_f\times C$, with $A\to B$ given by the pair of the localization and completion maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], applied to the multiplicative subset $\{1,f,f^2,\ldots\}$, the first factor $A_f$ is flat over $A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], applied to the Noetherian ring $A$ and ideal $(f)$, the second factor $C$ is flat over $A$. No local-ring hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tags 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), part (1), and 00MB (lemma-completion-flat), part (1); inputs of the cover in flat.tex Tag 05FS

proof.text: The $A$-module underlying $B$ has componentwise scalar multiplication through the two canonical maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules] with two factors and their flatness from Step 1. It gives that $B$ is flat as an $A$-module, hence that the displayed ring map $A\to B$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 05FS (lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective), proof, displayed localization-completion cover; product flatness input

proof.text: Let $\mathfrak m$ be any maximal ideal of $A$, and first suppose $f\notin\mathfrak m$. In the nonzero field $k=A/\mathfrak m$ write $\bar a$ for the class of $a$. The formula $a/f^n\mapsto\bar a\bar f^{-n}$ defines a unital ring map $A_f\to k$: the fraction equality in [def-weil-ring-localization-away] implies $\bar f^r(\bar a\bar f^m-\bar b\bar f^n)=0$, and division by powers of the nonzero $\bar f$ gives equality of the proposed values; the addition and multiplication formulas give preservation of both operations. Compose with $B\to A_f$. This map sends the image of every $a\in\mathfrak m$ to zero, so it kills the generated ideal $\mathfrak mB$. Since it sends $1$ to $1\ne0$, that ideal is proper.

source.place: Tag 00CO (definition-localization), fraction formulas; verification of the Tag 00HP maximal-ideal test for the cover in flat.tex Tag 05FS

proof.text: Now suppose $f\in\mathfrak m$. The ideal $(f)$ is finitely generated, by $f$. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] supplies the projection $\pi:C\to A/(f)$ whose composite with $A\to C$ is the quotient map. Because $(f)\subseteq\mathfrak m$, reduction defines a unital map $A/(f)\to A/\mathfrak m$. Compose $B\to C\xrightarrow{\pi}A/(f)\to A/\mathfrak m$. Its composite with $A\to B$ is reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$, so it kills every generator of $\mathfrak mB$ and hence the whole ideal. Again it sends $1$ to the nonzero element $1$ of $A/\mathfrak m$, so $\mathfrak mB\ne B$.

source.place: Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated), n=1; the same projection argument occurs in Tag 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), proof

proof.text: Step 2 proves that $A\to B$ is flat. Steps 3 and 4 cover every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$ and prove $\mathfrak mB\ne B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-faithfully-flat-maximal-ideals] to this map. It is faithfully flat, as asserted. The proof does not require $f$ to be a nonzerodivisor: the fraction argument only divides by its nonzero image in the residue field in the case where $f\notin\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00HP (lemma-ff), implication (4) to (1), for M=B; concludes the cover assertion of flat.tex Tag 05FS
